title: Question 8
stem:
The circuit of an inverting amplifier incorporating an ideal operational amplifier (op-amp) is shown
in Fig. 8.1.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why point P is known as a virtual earth.

markscheme_points.text: V+ is at earth potential so P (or V-) must be at earth

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in operational amplifiers that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
parts.proper_answer: op-amp has infinite/(very) large gain; op-amp saturates if V + ≠ V -; V+ is at earth potential so P (or V-) must be at earth
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Operational amplifiers. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
op-amp has infinite/(very) large gain; op-amp saturates if V + ≠ V -; V+ is at earth potential so P (or V-) must be at earth
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Derive an expression, in terms of the resistances $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$, for the gain of the amplifier
circuit.
Explain your working.

markscheme_points.text: input resistance to op-amp is very large or current in R2 = current in R1

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in operational amplifiers that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
parts.proper_answer: input resistance to op-amp is very large or current in R2 = current in R1; VIN (- 0) = IR2 and (0) - VOUT = IR1; VOUT / VIN = -R1 / R2

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
A relay and the output terminals of the amplifier circuit are shown in Fig. 8.2.
On Fig. 8.2, show how the relay may be connected to the amplifier output so that the relay
operates only when $V_{\mathrm{OUT}}$ is positive.

markscheme_points.text: relay coil connected between VOUT and earth
correct diode symbol connected between VOUT and coil or between coil and earth

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in A Level Physics theory and principles that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
parts.proper_answer: relay coil connected between VOUT and earth; correct diode symbol connected between VOUT and coil or between coil and earth; correct polarity for diode (‘clockwise’)
